name: Pediatric retrograde ESIN entries for proximal femoral fractures
aliases: ESIN entry points for pediatric proximal femur
retrograde elastic nailing entries for proximal femur
corridor: Paired medial and lateral distal-metaphyseal windows 2 cm above the distal femoral physis, with an optional second lateral portal 1.5 cm more proximal

positioning.text: Position supine with the knee and distal femur accessible and the femur imageable on orthogonal views.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the distal femoral physis and plan medial and first-lateral entries 2 cm above it; if a third nail is needed, mark a second lateral entry 1.5 cm proximal to the first lateral portal.

incision.text: Start an incision at each planned entry and extend it 2–4 cm distally, sized to the child.

superficial_interval.text: Divide subcutaneous tissues by blunt dissection to the medial and lateral femoral cortices.

deep_interval.text: Create cortical entries at the marked metaphyseal points, directed away from the open distal femoral physis.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, medial or lateral fascia and muscle, periosteum, distal metaphyseal cortex, then the medullary canal.

structures_at_risk.text: The distal femoral physis is the principal structure at risk if the portal is too close to the growth plate.

danger_zones.text: Keep the primary entries 2 cm above the physis; a third nail uses a second lateral portal 1.5 cm more proximal rather than crowding the growth plate.

retraction_hazards.text: Use blunt dissection to bone; avoid plunging toward the physis or trapping soft tissue around the nails.

exposure.text: Provides minimally invasive distal entries for retrograde elastic nails, preserving proximal soft tissues and facilitating early joint motion.

limitations.text: The corridor is an entry technique for selected proximal femoral fractures treated with ESIN; it does not expose the hip.

indications.text: Used for retrograde elastic nailing of selected pediatric proximal femoral fractures.

closure.text: Close subcutaneous tissue and skin according to surgeon preference.

complications.text: Complications include physeal injury from a portal that is too close to the growth plate.

procedure_applications.condition: A selected pediatric proximal femoral fracture is treated with retrograde elastic nails through distal metaphyseal entries

questions.question: How far above the physis are the medial and first lateral ESIN entries?
Where is a third nail inserted?
questions.answer: Through a second lateral entry 1.5 cm proximal to the first lateral portal.

questions.question: In which direction does each incision extend from the entry?
questions.answer: Distally, 2–4 cm depending on the size of the child.
